# Sony

## Brand Overview

Sony pioneered the full-frame mirrorless market with the original A7 in 2013 and has maintained a leading position ever since. All Sony mirrorless cameras -- both APS-C (Alpha 6000 series) and full-frame (Alpha 7/9 series) -- share a single **E-mount**. This is a significant advantage: FF lenses work on APS-C bodies (with a 1.5x crop), and the entire lens ecosystem is interchangeable across sensor sizes. Sony is widely regarded as the industry leader in autofocus (especially real-time eye/face tracking) and sensor technology, and offers the broadest native lens selection of any mirrorless system.

## Recommended Camera Bodies

Selected for people photography (portraits, burst for expressions) with weight as a priority.

| Model | Sensor | Resolution | Weight (g) | Cost (USD) | Burst (mech/elec fps) | AF (eye/face) | EVF | IBIS | Battery (CIPA) |
|-------|--------|-----------|------------|------------|----------------------|---------------|-----|------|----------------|
| A7C II | FF | 33 MP | 514 | ~$2,000 | 10 / 10 | Real-time Eye AF (human, animal, bird) | 2.36M dot OLED, 0.70x | 7-stop, 5-axis | ~530 (EVF) |
| A7 IV | FF | 33 MP | 658 | ~$2,500 | 10 / 10 | Real-time Eye AF (human, animal, bird) | 3.69M dot OLED, 0.78x | 5.5-stop, 5-axis | ~520 (EVF) |
| A9 III | FF | 24.6 MP | 702 | ~$6,000 | 30 / 120 | Real-time Eye AF (human, animal, bird); AI tracking | 9.44M dot OLED, 0.90x | 8-stop, 5-axis | ~400 (EVF) |
| A6700 | APS-C | 26 MP | 493 | ~$1,400 | 11 / 11 | Real-time Eye AF (human, animal, bird); AI tracking | 2.36M dot OLED, 1.07x (0.70x equiv) | 5-stop, 5-axis | ~550 (EVF) |

**Notes:**
- The **A7C II** is the lightest FF body Sony offers -- only 21g heavier than the APS-C A6700 -- making it the top pick when weight matters.
- The **A7 IV** adds a larger EVF and dual card slots (CFexpress A + SD) for a more traditional body.
- The **A9 III** features the world's first global shutter sensor: 120fps blackout-free burst, flash sync at any speed, and zero rolling shutter. Overkill for most portrait work but unmatched for capturing fleeting expressions.
- The **A6700** is Sony's flagship APS-C, sharing the same AI-based AF processor as the A7C II / A7R V.

## Lens Recommendations

### Prime Lenses

**35mm equivalent:**
- FF: Sony FE 35mm f/1.4 GM (SEL35F14GM)
- APS-C: Sony E 24mm f/1.8 ZA (SEL24F18Z) -- provides 36mm equiv

**50mm equivalent:**
- FF: Sony FE 50mm f/1.4 GM (SEL50F14GM)
- APS-C: Sony E 35mm f/1.8 OSS (SEL35F18) -- provides 52.5mm equiv

**85mm equivalent:**
- FF: Sony FE 85mm f/1.4 GM II (SEL85F14GM2)
- APS-C: Sony E 50mm f/1.8 OSS (SEL50F18) -- provides 75mm equiv (closest native option; no native APS-C ~56mm exists)

### Zoom Lens (24-70mm equivalent)
- FF: Sony FE 24-70mm f/2.8 GM II (SEL2470GM2)
- APS-C: Sony E 16-55mm f/2.8 G (SEL1655G) -- provides 24-82.5mm equiv

## Key Strengths and Weaknesses

**Strengths:**
- Best-in-class autofocus: real-time eye/face tracking is fast, accurate, and reliable across the entire lineup, from the $1,400 A6700 to the $6,000 A9 III.
- Single E-mount across APS-C and FF simplifies lens investment and allows gradual upgrades from APS-C to FF without replacing glass.
- Lightest FF body in the market (A7C II at 514g) is barely heavier than competing APS-C cameras.
- Deepest native lens ecosystem of any mirrorless system, with strong first-party (GM, G) and third-party (Sigma, Tamron, Samyang) options.

**Weaknesses:**
- APS-C lens lineup is aging: most native APS-C primes (E 24/1.8, E 35/1.8, E 50/1.8) are 10+ years old with slower AF motors and no weather sealing.
- The A7C II's compact body compromises ergonomics (small grip, small EVF) compared to the A7 IV; extended portrait sessions may cause hand fatigue.
- Sony's pricing is at a premium, especially for GM lenses and flagship bodies like the A9 III.
- Menu system, though improved in recent bodies (A7C II, A6700), still has a steeper learning curve than Canon or Nikon equivalents.
